title: LMDB block store backend
description:
Implement LmdbBlockStore using LMDB (Lightning Memory-Mapped Database) as a block store backend. LMDB is memory-mapped, ACID, and has extremely fast read performance — well suited to the newsreader workload (high read, moderate write).

Depends on: stoa-5c9f1a38 (pluggable backend selector).

## Why

LMDB's memory-mapped architecture means reads are effectively a `memcpy` from a mapped file. No serialization, no user/kernel boundary crossing for reads after the first page fault. For a newsreader serving hundreds of concurrent `ARTICLE` commands, this is meaningful. The `heed` crate provides idiomatic safe Rust bindings.

## What needs doing

- Add `heed` crate to Cargo.toml (LMDB bindings; links against system liblmdb or bundles it)
- Add `[backend.lmdb]` config section: `path` (directory for the LMDB environment), `map_size_gb` (virtual address space reservation; default 1 TB on 64-bit — does not pre-allocate disk)
- Implement `LmdbStore: IpfsStore` and `LmdbBlockStore: IpfsBlockStore`
  - One named database: `blocks`, key = CID bytes (`Cid::to_bytes()`), value = raw block bytes
  - `put`: `txn.put(db, &cid_bytes, &data, PutFlags::NO_OVERWRITE)` — idempotent
  - `get`: `txn.get(db, &cid_bytes)` — zero-copy read from mapped memory
  - `delete`: `txn.delete(db, &cid_bytes)` — for GC
  - delete returns DeletionOutcome::Immediate — key is removed as soon as the write transaction commits; get() returns NotFound immediately
- IPNS: disable
- Startup: open or create the environment; verify map_size is sufficient; emit warning if approaching 80% of map_size
- Note: LMDB write transactions are exclusive; concurrent writes serialize automatically

## GC / delete semantics

DeletionOutcome::Immediate. LMDB write transactions are synchronous. No grace period. The article is inaccessible as soon as the transaction commits. Note: LMDB does not immediately return freed pages to the OS — the data file does not shrink until the environment is compacted (mdb_copy or a compact-on-open flag). This is a storage accounting concern, not a data accessibility concern.

## Acceptance criteria
- Round-trip test using a tempdir environment
- Concurrent read test: 10 tokio tasks reading the same CID simultaneously with no contention errors
- Map size test: confirm startup fails with a clear error if the directory is not writable
- delete() removes the key; get() returns NotFound immediately after
- delete() on a CID that does not exist returns Ok(DeletionOutcome::Immediate) without error (idempotent)
